learning_outcomes.text: Acquires a knowledge base based on scientific, technological, and economic criteria about the different processes and manufacturing systems without chip removal.
Identifies some advantages and disadvantages, as well as defects and means of control and their solution.

Knows the machines, as well as the basic design principles of some tooling used in molding and deformation processes such as molds (metallic and disposable) and single and multi-stage dies for presses.
Selects appropriate manufacturing processes based on knowledge of their capabilities and limitations, according to technological, technical, and economic demands of both product and market.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to non-chip removal processes and their classification
Pre-forming processes by molding, casting, and injection
Forming processes by plastic deformation of metals (fundamentals, rolling, forging, extrusion and drawing, sheet and tube forming)
Joining and assembly processes in metal-mechanical constructions
Laboratory/room practices: Six three-hour sessions on: metal deformation forming, joining in metal constructions, molding and casting, and quality engineering tools.
teaching_methods: Theory classes, numerical estimations, and/or practical cases in the classroom
Optional visits to trade fairs or technological events, as well as to manufacturing, installation and/or assembly companies

assessment_methods.method: Practical reports (after attendance) during the course

assessment_rules: A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in each assessment activity (written tests for each of the two parts of the exam and each practical session) to be able to average and pass the course; otherwise, the total grade will be 3.9 or lower. Grades below 5 points in the whole or parts of the exam in the 1st call are NOT retained for the 2nd call. Students who do not pass the practical part (failure to complete and/or submit all reports in the correct format and by the deadline) will have to take an additional related test (exam) during the global evaluation.
